**Getting started**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## What is the Occam's Variant Grammar?

It's a standardized, tab-separated representation of small and structural DNA
variants as well as RNA variants that VSTOL converts every supported caller's VCF into, so that variants
from different callers can be compared and combined. Each variant is described by
two breakpoints (`chromosome_1`/`position_1` and `chromosome_2`/`position_2`)
with strands and operations. See the
[introduction](https://pirlblog.substack.com/p/variant-standardization) for the
full rationale.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Which variant callers does `vcf2tsv` support?

A wide range of small-variant and structural-variant callers (Clair3, ClairS,
cuteSV, DeepVariant, DeepSomatic, Delly2, Dysgu, GRIDSS2, HaplotypeCaller,
Longshot, Lumpy, Manta, Mutect2, NanoCaller, Nanomonsv, NanoVar, PBSV, Savana,
Severus, Sniffles2, Strelka2, SVIM, SVision-pro, and more). Pass the caller via
`--method`; run `vstol vcf2tsv --help` for the current list, or see the
[README](https://github.com/pirl-unc/vstol) for tested versions.
:::

**Operations**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## How does VSTOL decide that two variants are "the same"?

The matching commands (`diff`, `intersect`, `merge`) share three options:

- `--max-breakpoint-distance` — two breakpoints within this distance (inclusive)
  are treated as the same position.
- `--match-both-positions` — whether *both* breakpoint pairs must match, or just
  one.
- `--match-operation-types` — whether the operation types must also match.

Small variants (SNVs, MNVs, small indels up to `--max-small-var-size`) must match
positions exactly and ignore `--max-breakpoint-distance`, so distinct nearby
point mutations are not clustered together.
:::
